title: Optical phased array
title_note: The letter calls it "a novel focusing and dispersive component ... based on a phased array of bent optical waveguides" (Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.385); it uses neither "PHASAR" nor "arrayed-waveguide grating". The name arrayed-waveguide grating appears in the title of Takahashi et al., Electron. Lett. 1990, p.87. A later review by the same author calls this letter "the first AWG" (Smit et al., Semicond. Sci. Technol. 2014, p.2); the 1988 letter itself says only "novel".
tagline: Thirty-one bent Al₂O₃ guides focus and disperse light like a grating.

parts.name: silicon substrate
parts.role: Silicon wafer under the Al₂O₃ guides; size not stated (stand-in).
parts.detail: The arrays were realised "using Al_{2}O_{3} ridge guides on a silicon substrate, as described in References 4 and 5" (Smit, van der Laan and Acket, Thin Solid Films 1986; Smit, Sensors & Actuators symposium 1986). Neither reference is read here, so the layer stack (film thickness, ridge height, any buffer layer) is withheld. Substrate size is not stated: drawn as a plain stand-in.
parts.quote: We realised a set of arrays using Al_{2}O_{3} ridge guides on a silicon substrate, as described in References 4 and 5.

geometry.note: plain rectangle framing the five arrays; size not stated

parts.name: further arrays
parts.role: Four more identical arrays on the same substrate.
parts.detail: Fig. 3 shows "five identical arrays (the white areas)" in a column; the second one is excited. Centre-to-centre pitch read from the photograph against its 1 mm bar: about 0.50 mm (65.4 px at 131 px/mm, spread 63-67 px). Each white area measures about 0.5-0.6 mm across and 0.3-0.37 mm high, consistent with the stated radii and sector angle. In the photograph each array sits about 0.07 mm left of the one above (about 0.27 mm over the column; a stagger or a slight tilt of the column, not stated); drawn aligned (assumed).
parts.quote: The substrate comprises five identical arrays (the white areas).
parts.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.385 col. 2 to p.386 col. 1; Fig. 3 (p.386)

geometry.direction: y; one copy above the excited array, three below (the excited one is the second from the top)

dims.label: array pitch
dims.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, Fig. 3 (p.386), against the 1 mm bar
dims.note: read from a halftone photograph, about ±0.03 mm

parts.name: phased array
parts.role: Concentric bent Al₂O₃ ridge guides; drawn equidistant (true radii not printed).
parts.detail: 31 concentric waveguides, 3 µm wide, at an average radial spacing of 6 µm, with bending radii R_{i} from 910 to 1090 µm, each turning through the sector angle ψ = 30°. The guides are deliberately not equidistant: the radii are computed from βψR_{i} = Φ(R_{i}) + 2πm_{i} (Eq. (3)) so that each guide delivers a chosen phase; the m_{i} are picked to keep the array as close to equidistant as possible. The individual radii and the phase profile used are not printed, so the guides are drawn equidistant at the stated 6 µm average (the stated example, m_{i} - m_{i-1} = 10, needs spacing changes of at most ±5 %).
parts.quote: We chose a number of 31 concentric waveguides with a width of 3 µm at an average distance ΔR_{i} of 6 µm, R_{i} varying between 910 and 1090 µm. ψ was chosen 30°.
parts.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.386 col. 1; Fig. 1 and Eq. (3) (p.385)

radius_um.drawn: equidistant at the stated average; true radii not printed

geometry.note: guide i is the arc (R_{i} sin θ, -R_{i} cos θ), θ from 0 (input plane, heading +x) to 30° (output plane, heading 30° above +x); true scale

dims.label: average gap between guides
dims.locator: 6 µm spacing - 3 µm width (Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.386 col. 1)

dims.label: plan extent of one array
dims.locator: from the radii and ψ; Fig. 3 white areas measure about 0.5-0.6 × 0.3-0.37 mm

parts.name: input plane
parts.role: Radial line where all guides start, facing the incoming beam.
parts.detail: Fig. 1 labels the straight radial line through the centre of curvature where every guide begins "input plane". The guides start there tangent to the incoming beam direction. The phase at the input plane, φ_{0}, is the same for all guides and drops out (Eq. (1)). No fan-in section: the letter recommends adding "fan-in and fan-out coupling sections" to avoid multiple orders and reduce coupling losses, which this device did not have.
parts.quote: To avoid the occurrence of multiple orders, and simultaneously reduce coupling losses, the array should be provided with fan-in and fan-out coupling sections.
parts.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, Fig. 1 and Eq. (1) (p.385); p.386 col. 1

parts.name: output plane
parts.role: Radial line at the sector angle where all guides end.
parts.detail: Fig. 1 labels the radial line at the sector angle ψ "output plane". Light arrives there with phase φ_{i} = βψR_{i} + φ_{0} (Eq. (1)): every guide turns through the same angle, so the path, and the phase, grows linearly with the radius. Guide ends lie at the 6 µm average spacing along this line; light leaves each guide along its tangent, perpendicular to the line.
parts.quote: The light coupled into the waveguides will propagate to the output plane and arrive there with phase distribution
parts.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.385 col. 1; Fig. 1 and Eq. (1) (p.385)

geometry.note: radial at θ = 30°; inner guide end (455.0, -788.1), outer (545.0, -944.0)

parts.name: sector angle ψ
parts.role: Angle every guide turns through, between input and output planes.
parts.detail: ψ is "the sector angle of the concentric array" (Fig. 1). The experiment used ψ = 30°. ψ also sets the dispersion: Eq. (4) gives dα ≈ ψ dβ/β, "a wavelength shift of 1 % will cause an angular dispersion of 0.01ψ; with ψ = π this is roughly 2°".
parts.quote: ψ is the sector angle of the concentric array, and R_{i} is the bending radius of the ith waveguide.
parts.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.385 col. 2; Fig. 1, Eq. (4) (p.385); p.386 col. 1

geometry.note: drawn at the centre of curvature between the two radial planes, as in Fig. 1

parts.name: broad Gaussian He-Ne beam
parts.role: Broad He-Ne beam over the input plane; λ 0.6320 µm as printed.
parts.detail: The second array of Fig. 3 "is excited with a broad Gaussian He-Ne beam (λ = 0.6320 µm)" (wavelength as printed; the common He-Ne line is 0.6328 µm). "Part of the incident power will couple into the waveguides and the other part will propagate straight forward or be scattered" (p.385). How the beam was launched into the film and its width are not stated; drawn as a parallel band covering the input plane.
parts.quote: the second array, which is excited with a broad Gaussian He-Ne beam (λ = 0.6320 µm)
parts.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.386 col. 1; p.385 col. 1

geometry.profile: Gaussian across the band (stated "Gaussian"; width not stated)

parts.name: uncoupled light
parts.role: Light that misses the guides and runs straight on.
parts.detail: Not all of the broad beam enters the guides: "the other part will propagate straight forward or be scattered" (p.385). Fig. 3 shows a bright horizontal streak continuing past the excited array at its height. Fraction not stated.
parts.quote: part of the incident power will couple into the waveguides and the other part will propagate straight forward or be scattered.
parts.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.385 col. 1; Fig. 3 (p.386)

parts.name: region beyond the output plane
parts.role: Where the beams from the guides converge toward the focal plane.
parts.detail: Between the output plane and the focal plane the beams leave the guides and converge; Fig. 3 shows them as a bright fan rising at about 29° from the horizontal (measured on the photograph), close to the 30° sector angle. The layer makeup of this region is not stated.

geometry.corners: output plane ends (455.0, -788.1), (545.0, -944.0) to the focal plane ±150 µm around the focus
geometry.note: outline only as the support for the converging beams

parts.name: focal plane
parts.role: Design focal plane, 1 mm beyond the output plane.
parts.detail: A quadratic phase distribution Φ(R_{i}) "will yield a focusing operation" (p.385). In Fig. 3 "the dashed line represents the design position for the focal plane (f = 1 mm)". On the photograph the dashed line lies about 0.95-1.05 mm from the excited array and roughly perpendicular to the outgoing beams. The focus is drawn on the perpendicular through the middle of the output plane; the centre of the quadratic profile is not printed.
parts.quote: The dashed line represents the design position for the focal plane (f = 1 mm).
parts.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.386 col. 1; Fig. 3 (p.386); p.385 col. 2

geometry.note: axis from the output-plane midpoint (500.0, -866.0) along (0.866, 0.5) for f = 1000 µm

parts.name: focused orders
parts.role: Several foci side by side, one per grating order; drawn count illustrative.
parts.detail: "A phased array having different orders and multiple foci will occur without additional measures"; Fig. 3 shows "a number of focused beams emerging from the second array". The spacing of the orders in the focal plane "compares well with the theoretically expected value (66 µm)". The number of orders seen is not stated: drawn are the central focus and one neighbour on each side (illustrative count). Spot size not stated.
parts.quote: The spatial separation of the orders in the focal plane compares well with the theoretically expected value (66 µm).
parts.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.386 col. 1; Fig. 3 (p.386)

geometry.note: central brightest, neighbours fainter (relative strengths not stated); count illustrative

dims.label: order separation (theory)
dims.note: theoretical value; the measured spacing is said to compare well, no number printed

parts.name: tilted wavefront
parts.role: Wavelength shift tilts the wavefront, moving the focus; shift drawn 10× larger.
parts.detail: The channel length is proportional to R_{i}, so a frequency shift causes a phase shift linear in R_{i}: "the position of the focus in the focal plane will shift linearly with df, the focal length remaining unaffected" (p.385). Fig. 2 relates the wavefront tilt α to the phase step Δφ_{i} between neighbouring guides; Eq. (4): dα ≈ ψ dβ/β, so a 1 % wavelength shift tilts the beam by 0.01ψ. For this array (ψ = 30°, f = 1 mm) that is about 0.3°, about 5 µm along the focal plane per 1 % (derived, not printed). Drawn shift is exaggerated. Direction (derived from Eq. (1), not stated): a longer wavelength moves the focus toward the inner, smaller-radius side.
parts.quote: Consequently, the position of the focus in the focal plane will shift linearly with df, the focal length remaining unaffected.
parts.locator: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, p.385 col. 2; Fig. 2 and Eq. (4) (p.385)

geometry.note: short lines parallel to the output plane, then tilted; focus slides along the focal plane; magnitude exaggerated and labelled

dims.label: focus shift for this array

parts.name: five-channel demultiplexer prototype
parts.role: 1.3 × 4 mm prototype; its layout is not printed.
parts.detail: The dispersion separates wavelengths "by positioning a set of receiver waveguides next to each other in the focal plane". A "small size (1.3 × 4 mm) five-channel demultiplexer prototype working at He-Ne wavelength with a wavelength channel spacing of 0.5 %" showed "good focusing properties and a channel separation better than 20 dB". The prototype's array (guide count, radii, sector angle, focal length), the receiver-guide positions and spacing, the five wavelengths and how they were produced are not printed: drawn as a plain outline only, interior withheld. 0.5 % of 0.6320 µm is about 3.2 nm (derived).
parts.quote: We realised a small size (1.3 × 4 mm) five-channel demultiplexer prototype working at He-Ne wavelength with a wavelength channel spacing of 0.5%, exhibiting good focusing properties and a channel separation better than 20 dB.
parts.material: Al₂O₃ ridge guides on silicon (as the arrays; not restated for the prototype)

chapters.line: Al_{2}O_{3} ridge guides on a silicon substrate.
chapters.action: plan view from above: silicon stand-in, five pale sector-shaped arrays in a column at the measured pitch (Fig. 3 white areas); the zoom toward the second from the top opens the bends chapter, so the chapter ends on all five

chapters.line: 31 guides bend around one shared centre.
chapters.action: other arrays fade; the 31 arcs draw in one by one from the input plane to the output plane at true scale (radii 910-1090 µm, 3 µm wide, drawn equidistant at 6 µm); input and output planes appear as dash-dot radial lines

chapters.line: Same sector angle, so path length grows with radius.
chapters.action: sector-angle arc appears at the centre of curvature; innermost and outermost guides highlight in turn to show length ψR_{i} growing linearly with radius

chapters.line: Radii set so phases align; a quadratic profile focuses.
chapters.action: small phase ticks (one per guide) appear at the output plane: first aligned (Eq. (2)), then bending into a shallow parabola (Eq. (3), quadratic Φ); no numbers; true radii stay drawn equidistant (hover says why)

chapters.line: A wide He-Ne beam lights the guides; some runs straight on.
chapters.action: red Gaussian band enters from the left across the whole input plane; light runs along the arcs from input to output plane; a faint part continues straight on past the array (uncoupled light)

chapters.line: Beams converge on the focal plane, in several orders.
chapters.action: light leaves each guide perpendicular to the output plane and converges across the free region onto the dashed focal plane; the central focus brightens, with fainter neighbouring orders 66 µm to each side (count illustrative)

chapters.line: A wavelength shift tilts the wavefront; the focus slides sideways.
chapters.action: model frames left, plot assembles right; wavefront lines at the output plane tilt (Fig. 2) and the central focus slides along the focal plane in step with the plot pen (position from the plotted point, exaggerated on the model and labelled so in hover), focal length unchanged; longer wavelength toward the inner (smaller-radius) side; never beyond ±1 %

chapters.line: Receiver guides in the focal plane; prototype layout not printed.
chapters.action: model frames left; a plain outline of the 1.3 × 4 mm prototype fades in beside it, interior empty (layout withheld); hover / panel give five channels, 0.5 % spacing, channel separation better than 20 dB

plots.label: Eq. (4)
plots.source: Smit, Electron. Lett. 1988, Eq. (4) (p.385 col. 2): dα ≈ ψ dβ/β; a 1 % wavelength shift gives 0.01ψ
plots.note: Computed from Eq. (4), not measured. + = toward the inner guides for a longer wavelength (direction derived, not stated). Model shift drawn 10× larger. Shift along the focal line = f × ψ × (Δλ/λ), with the printed ψ = 30° and f = 1 mm of the Fig. 3 arrays (not the demultiplexer prototype, whose design is not printed); |dβ/β| taken as |Δλ/λ|, as the letter's 1 % example does. Range ±1 %, the shift the letter discusses; neighbouring orders (66 µm away) lie far outside it. The letter prints no measured dispersion. Sampled every 1/30 % (61 points, 1/60 of the axis span).
